system.name: EROICA
system.one_liner: online performance troubleshooting for large-scale model training that detects slowdowns without source-code instrumentation

content.key_idea: EROICA first learns a training job's iteration boundary from a repeating D/O event pattern, then continuously re-checks that pattern's timing, falling back to re-detection if the pattern ever stops matching for too long.

summary: This figure is a flowchart of EROICA's two-phase iteration- and degradation-detection loop. In Iteration Detection, EROICA buffers a recent D/O event sequence, shown concretely as 'D D O O D', and checks whether M identical repeats have occurred; once found, the training-iteration pattern is identified and handed to Performance degradation detection. That stage keeps its own worked event buffer and checks whether a full iteration has just completed. A completed iteration's duration is checked against a degradation threshold, triggering Start Profiling on a hit or otherwise resuming monitoring; an incomplete iteration is checked against a K-event stall limit, which either resumes monitoring or sends the process back to Iteration Detection to re-learn the pattern. The concrete D/O sequences inside both boxes ground the abstract sliding-window logic in a traceable example.
